why: the machine was rebooted between rounds. The Codex CLI had been upgraded in place, so the declared toolchain pin named a binary that no longer existed, and every lane dispatch failed BEFORE SPAWNING with ERR_LANE_PIN_IDENTITY_INVALID / ERR_LANE_TOOLCHAIN_BINARY_MISSING. The SBL EXECUTE and VERIFY lanes could not run at all -- including the independent acceptance officer.

defect_1_toolchain_pin.method: path DISCOVERED under %LOCALAPPDATA%/OpenAI/Codex/bin; version from `codex.exe --version`; digest computed over the installed file. The registry's /codex_version and /codex_sha256 expected values were re-pinned in the SAME commit; the pointer POSITIONS were not moved.
defect_1_toolchain_pin.verified_by: hgk-lane-toolchain.py -> ok: true (path, version and digest all match)
defect_1_toolchain_pin.evidence_not_rewritten: the probe receipts under evidence/ still record what the lane served on 2026-10-21 with the OLD build; they are history and remain true

defect_2_stale_selection_note.what: all three lanes' selection_note still read 'minimax-m3.1-flash-free (opencode-go) is rank 1', contradicting the same file's declared_by, change_log and ordered_pool[0]
defect_2_stale_selection_note.why_it_mattered: a reviewer reading the note would conclude MiniMax was the PLAN binding -- exactly the lane-vs-session confusion the owner ordered to be avoided
defect_2_stale_selection_note.fix: the note is now GENERATED from ordered_pool[0], so it cannot drift again

session_interaction_plane.role: the interactive session; NOT the PLAN lane binding

lane_planes_are_separate.note: the two are separate planes; the session pin is never used as the PLAN binding, and the pool's rank-1 arms are the lane bindings

claim_ceiling: these are MAKER-side measurements of the maker's own lane configuration, taken by running the lanes. The independent acceptance of the SBL product candidate is a SEPARATE verdict and is not claimed here.
